name: ANSI single-pole switch plan symbol
summary: US-style plan symbol for a single-pole wall switch: the letter S at the switch position with a switch leg to the lights.
description: US architectural electrical plans mark a single-pole wall switch with the letter S beside the wall, usually with a short line to the wall. A curved dashed switch leg runs to the controlled lighting outlets, and lowercase letters can tie a switch to specific fixtures.

Subscripts modify the S: S3 for three-way, S4 for four-way, SD for dimmer, SK for key-operated and so on. The plain S therefore means a basic single-pole switch. The S does not say rating, colour or device style, which are specified separately.
readingNotes: Check for subscripts that change the type.
Follow switch legs or lowercase letters to the controlled fixtures.
drawingChecklist: Draw switch legs or letter keys to fixtures.
State mounting height in general notes.
distinction: The IEC one-way switch is drawn as a circle with a stroke; the US form is the letter S.
